_about: Potemkin skill data plane. Math foundations, constraint taxonomy, state machine schema, termination limits, reparameterization move catalog.

math_foundations._about: Named mathematical frameworks this skill operationalizes. Agent reads these on Phase 0 load.

CSP.definition: Triple (X, D, C): X = variables, D = domains (possible values per variable), C = constraints (relations that must hold between variable assignments)
CSP.solution: Assignment a: X → D such that every c ∈ C evaluates true under a
CSP.violation_function: V(a, C) = { c ∈ C | c(a) = false } - the set of currently violated constraints
CSP.how_potemkin_uses_it: The blocked problem is modeled as a CSP. The solver's current attempt is an assignment a. Potemkin extracts V(a, C), names the violated constraints, and searches for a new assignment.

Kleene_fixed_point.origin: Stephen Cole Kleene - Introduction to Metamathematics, 1952
Kleene_fixed_point.definition: For a monotone function F on a complete lattice (L, ≤), the least fixed point exists and equals the limit of iterating F from bottom: ⊥, F(⊥), F(F(⊥)), ...
Kleene_fixed_point.fixed_point_condition: F(x) = x - output equals input, no further change
Kleene_fixed_point.convergence: If F is monotone and the lattice is complete, iteration terminates at the least fixed point
Kleene_fixed_point.how_potemkin_uses_it: F = reparameterize(s, extract_violated(s, C)). Each iteration produces a tighter solution candidate. Iteration stops when F(s) = s (fixpoint, all constraints satisfied) or the domain collapses to ∅ (infeasible). Kleene guarantees this terminates if the constraint set is finite.

Lyapunov_stability.origin: Aleksandr Lyapunov - The General Problem of the Stability of Motion, 1892
Lyapunov_stability.definition: A scalar function L(s) defined on the state space such that L(s) > 0 for all non-equilibrium states and L decreases strictly along every trajectory: L(s_{n+1}) < L(s_n)
Lyapunov_stability.convergence_guarantee: If such a function exists, the system must converge - it cannot cycle indefinitely
Lyapunov_stability.how_potemkin_uses_it: L(s) = |V(s, C)| = count of violated constraints. Every accepted potemkin iteration must reduce this count. If an iteration produces L_new >= L_current, it is rejected - the solver cannot accept a move that doesn't reduce violations. This is the anti-loop enforcement mechanism.
Lyapunov_stability.why_it_matters: Without a Lyapunov condition the agent can appear to be working while actually cycling. The strict decrease requirement makes looping structurally impossible - not a behavioral guideline.

BLOCKER.definition: Restricts the operation space - prevents a class of moves
identifies_as: solver says 'I can't do X because of Y'
constraint prevents reaching goal via current approach
constraint is phrased as a prohibition
BLOCKER.common_trap: assuming BLOCKER when constraint is actually RULER - check if constraint fixes a quantity before classifying

RULER.definition: Fixes a quantity or invariant - use as a tool, not an obstacle
identifies_as: constraint specifies an exact value, total, or conserved quantity
constraint says 'X must equal Y' or 'total is Z'
constraint defines a boundary the solution must be within, not excluded from
RULER.common_trap: ALT calls this same pattern - if potemkin cycles on a RULER, escalate to /ALT

HIDDEN.definition: Not stated explicitly - inferred from failure pattern
identifies_as: solver fails without being able to identify why
every attempt hits the same wall with no stated reason
assumption embedded in problem framing that was never surfaced
HIDDEN.extraction_method: inversion: what would have to be true for the current approach to be impossible?
HIDDEN.common_trap: mistaking HIDDEN for PHANTOM - if removing the constraint resolves the block, it was PHANTOM not HIDDEN

PHANTOM.definition: Apparent constraint that dissolves on examination
identifies_as: solver refuses to attempt something based on assumed impossibility
constraint was never stated but solver is behaving as if it exists
stated constraint doesn't actually apply to the current problem
PHANTOM.action: remove immediately from C - do not reparameterize around a phantom

ENTRY.description: Initial state. Problem and current solution attempt loaded.

PHASE_0_CAPTURE.description: State locked down. Failure point identified. L_initial computed.

REMOVE_PHANTOM.description: Phantom removed from C. L recalculated.

LYAPUNOV_PASS.description: Valid iteration. s and L updated.

LYAPUNOV_FAIL.description: Invalid iteration rejected. Return to Phase 2 with next move.

PHASE_4_INFEASIBLE.description: Terminal. Solution space empty or moves exhausted.

PHASE_4_CYCLE.description: Terminal. Same constraint appearing without L reduction.

PHASE_4_REFRAME.description: Terminal. Max iterations reached with partial progress.

dual_route.description: Find operation sequence achieving same goal without triggering constraint
dual_route.procedure: enumerate goal-preserving operations, filter out those blocked by C, select first valid

decompose.description: Break goal into sub-goals where constraint applies to only one sub-goal
decompose.procedure: identify which component of goal triggers constraint, isolate it, satisfy other components independently

relax.description: Identify which part of the goal can be relaxed while preserving core intent
relax.procedure: distinguish essential vs incidental properties of goal, attempt solution on essential properties only

use_invariant.description: Treat the fixed quantity as a computational tool
use_invariant.procedure: extract the fixed quantity Q, express goal in terms of Q, derive solution directly

invert_goal.description: Restate goal in terms of the fixed quantity
invert_goal.procedure: ask 'what assignment of variables, given Q is fixed, achieves the goal?'

interval_arithmetic.description: Compute what the fixed quantity implies for each variable's domain
interval_arithmetic.procedure: propagate constraint through variable domains, reduce domains to consistent intervals

make_explicit.description: Add surfaced constraint to C, recompute domain
make_explicit.procedure: state CONSTRAINT[n] formally, add to C, recalculate D given new C, verify satisfiability

check_consistency.description: Verify new C is satisfiable after adding hidden constraint
check_consistency.procedure: check for contradictions between CONSTRAINT[n] and existing C, if contradiction found escalate to INFEASIBLE

re_approach.description: Generate new solution attempt under explicit C
re_approach.procedure: with all constraints now explicit, restart search in constrained space

remove_from_C.procedure: delete from C, recalculate V(s, C), update L

verify_dissolution.description: Confirm constraint was phantom and not misclassified
verify_dissolution.procedure: after removal, check if original failure signal persists - if yes, re-examine classification

recalculate_L.description: Update Lyapunov count after phantom removal

limits.on_max_iter_exceeded: PHASE_4_REFRAME - not INFEASIBLE unless domain is empty

lyapunov.function: L(s) = |V(s, C)| = count of violated constraints
lyapunov.requirement: L(s_{n+1}) < L(s_n) for every accepted iteration
lyapunov.on_violation: reject s_{n+1}, return to PHASE_2_REPARAMETERIZE with next move
